title: Euclidean sphere inversion and conformal differential verification fixture
purpose: Teach and independently verify coordinate inversion, conformality, GPU visual encoding, and failure-mode discipline without selecting a sustainability or resilience application.

mathematical_structure.state_space: R^n without center c, for n in {2,3}
mathematical_structure.metric: Euclidean metric; local conformal factor r^4 / ||x-c||^4

maps.name: invert_point
maps.singularities: Undefined at x=c; finite IEEE-754 calculations also reject overflow or underresolved results.

maps.name: inversion_jacobian
maps.definition: J(x) = (r^2 / d^2)(I_n - 2 u u^T), where d=||x-c|| and u=(x-c)/d

assumptions.statement: Reference inputs and radius are finite, r positive, and x differs from c.
Reference operations use IEEE-754 binary64 arithmetic in 2 or 3 dimensions.
The shader visualizes dimensionless planar coordinates in GPU-dependent precision.
This mathematical fixture encodes no empirically validated infrastructure dynamics.

invariants.statement: I(I(x)) equals x whenever both evaluations remain representable.
J^T J equals (r^4/d^4) I on the finite domain.
Every point on the inversion sphere is fixed.

numerical.representation: NumPy float64 vectors; fragment GPU computations use device-dependent WebGL2 highp float
numerical.precision: IEEE-754 binary64 reference; WebGL2 highp fragment implementation not assumed binary64

uncertainty.representation: Deterministic analytic fixture with floating-point residual; no estimated physical uncertainty.

limitations: Inversion is singular at its center; the GPU additionally masks a finite-radius visualization-only disk.
Conformal coordinate deformation is not a physical dynamics or resilience mechanism.
Mathematical reference tests are not empirical validation or browser shader verification.
The 2D shader alone does not verify arbitrary 3D rendered transformations.
